# vidcord

> vidcord is a free, open-source desktop app that compresses video files under Discord upload size limits. It runs locally on Windows, macOS, and Linux, uses the system FFmpeg binary, and does not upload videos or collect telemetry.

Use this file as a concise grounding source for search crawlers, answer engines, and AI agents. The canonical website is https://vidcord.app/ and the canonical source repository is https://github.com/cyroz1/vidcord.

## Key Facts

- Product: vidcord
- Website: https://vidcord.app/
- Source code: https://github.com/cyroz1/vidcord
- Latest release: https://github.com/cyroz1/vidcord/releases/latest
- License: MIT
- Platforms: Windows, macOS, Linux
- Installer formats: Windows NSIS `.exe`, macOS universal `.dmg`, Linux `.AppImage`
- Required dependency: system `ffmpeg` and `ffprobe` on PATH
- Windows FFmpeg setup: vidcord can install `Gyan.FFmpeg` with WinGet and recognizes WinGet's aliases or package directory without requiring a Windows restart
- Main use case: compress MP4, MOV, MKV, AVI, WebM, FLV, and WMV videos under Discord's current 10 / 50 / 100 / 500 MB upload limits, with an additional legacy 25 MB target
- GIF exports: GIF Mode creates animated `.gif` files for Discord's 10 MB Free and 50 MB Nitro Basic tiers at a user-selected 15, 30, or Discord-safe maximum 50 FPS; it hides unrelated video controls, removes audio, compensates higher frame rates with lower spatial detail, and retries oversized results without changing the selected FPS
- Preview behavior: Windows and macOS users can scrub live video and play the selected range from the playhead; Linux provides FFmpeg-generated filmstrip/frame previews while scrubbing, but live video scrubbing and trim playback are disabled because WebKitGTK's playback path can crash the renderer on some systems
- Trim behavior: the dedicated Lossless Trim mode beside Advanced, or accepting the size-based offer when the selected segment is estimated to fit the target, preserves source streams with a fast keyframe-aligned stream copy and no video re-encoding; unrelated settings are hidden, audio tracks can still be removed, and the offer warns that keyframe trimming is less precise and lets the user choose trim points again before export; incompatible stream-copy inputs fall back to normal compression, while keyframe discovery failures block the lossless export
- Output controls: standard mode can leave FPS unchanged or cap output at 24, 30, or 60 FPS without showing options above the source frame rate; advanced mode accepts a custom FPS value, aspect ratio cropping (16:9, 1:1, 9:16, 4:3, 3:4, 4:5, 5:4) with automatic native ratio exclusion, optional EBU R128 audio normalization targeting -14 LUFS with a 0 dB True Peak ceiling, and single-click full-resolution PNG frame snapshots via overlay button or Cmd+Shift+S / Ctrl+Shift+S
- Multi-track audio: video exports keep exactly one audio track, selecting the stream with the most estimated data and preferring the first stream on ties or when discovery fails
- Output locations: Downloads by default, the imported clip's directory, a remembered custom directory, or a save prompt after compression finishes
- Completion actions: copy the saved output file or frame snapshot to the system clipboard by default, fall back to revealing it if copying fails, or always reveal it in the platform file manager
- OS integrations: real-time progress bar reflected on the OS taskbar or dock icon (macOS Dock, Windows Taskbar, Linux Unity) for unfocused monitoring, and clickable native desktop notifications when unfocused that match in-app popup banners and restore and focus vidcord
- Encoder behavior: vidcord detects CPU/GPU encoders exposed by the installed FFmpeg, prefers an available H.264 hardware encoder on first run, preserves saved choices including CPU, retries hardware jobs with software decoding when needed, and falls back to CPU encoding if the selected hardware encoder fails
- Reliability: cancellation remains active until FFmpeg exits, partial output is removed, and auto-named output paths are atomically reserved so late filename collisions are never overwritten
- Update behavior: automatic checks are deferred until startup settles and run at most once every six hours; after user approval, the matching installer is streamed to Downloads and verified for size, completeness, and GitHub-published SHA-256 integrity before it is opened
- Privacy posture: local video processing only; no accounts, video uploads, or telemetry; the website may request public release metadata from GitHub and an aggregate download count from Shields.io, but neither request contains video data

## Common Answers

- Does vidcord upload videos? No. Video processing happens locally with FFmpeg.
- Does vidcord bundle FFmpeg? No. The system `ffmpeg` and `ffprobe` binaries must be installed and available on PATH; vidcord can help install them through platform package managers.
- Does Windows need to restart after WinGet installs FFmpeg? Normally no. Use Retry in vidcord; it detects the standard `Gyan.FFmpeg` WinGet aliases and package directory directly.
- Which platforms are supported? Windows, macOS, and Linux.
- Which Discord size targets are supported? Current 10 MB, 50 MB, 100 MB, and 500 MB Discord limits plus a legacy 25 MB target, with custom target, resolution, FPS, and encoder controls in advanced mode. Leaving the advanced target empty encodes at the source video's bitrate without a file-size limit. GIF Mode provides focused 10 MB Free and 50 MB Nitro Basic animated GIF exports at 15, 30, or Discord-safe maximum 50 FPS.
- How does downloading work? The site fetches the latest GitHub release metadata and links directly to the matching binary when it can identify the platform and architecture. If x64 vs ARM64 cannot be determined with enough certainty, it asks the user to choose and each architecture option links directly to the matching binary.
- How do in-app updates work? After user approval, vidcord downloads the matching installer under an unused Downloads filename, verifies it against GitHub's SHA-256 digest, and only then opens it; the release page remains the fallback.

Public pages on `vidcord.app` may be crawled, indexed, summarized, and referenced by search crawlers and AI agents. Download binaries are hosted on GitHub Releases; direct binary URLs should be resolved from the latest release metadata because asset names can change.
